newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: French govt has "no problem" with dlr level-minister.
newsitem.headline: French govt has "no problem" with dlr level-minister.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said the French government had no problem with the dollar's current level.
He also told a press briefing the government still wanted Italy to be an early member of planned European economic and monetary union.
Strauss-Kahn said three of the four conditions set by his Socialist party for EMU had virtually been achieved.
"We didn't discuss this question but it will have to be addressed in the weeks and months ahead," he said.

"There were four elements. The first was the parity against the dollar. From that point of view, the dollar has moved in such a way that the problem is not topical, at least for the moment," the minister said.

"Second was an economic government for Europe. We're doing that now (with the resolution on growth and jobs). Thirdly, a solidarity and growth pact. When the modalities of this economic government, or in any case this economic pillar, are in place, we'll decide what name to give the resolution, and I will propose it be called a pact for solidarity and growth," Strauss-Kahn said.
That left the issue of the Socialists' call for Spain and Italy to be included in the first wave of EMU members, he said.
"That question wasn't discussed. This wasn't the time or place. But we continue to think that the euro must be able to include from the start Spain and Italy," he added.
